title: The Last Biscuit at Harbour Street
audience: adults who like gentle puzzles and small-town charm
premise: When the beloved biscuit tin disappears from Harbour Street Bakery on the morning of the town fair, retired librarian Mira Vale notices three clues nobody else sees — a floury footprint, a missing library key, and a note that smells like lavender. She has one day to find the thief before the fair ribbon-cutting.
tone: warm, lightly humorous, low-stakes suspense; clean prose with sensory bakery detail
